title: Shaan Puri's 3-step plan to figure out what you want: pop the bubble, wander, look for clues
summary: Shaan explains how to find a career you'll stick with through the "decade of suck": test-drive jobs before committing, take a time-boxed season of wandering, and hunt for clues (energy and blueprints). Love is framed as a competitive advantage because people who love it practice more.

principles.text: Test-drive your dream job for two weeks before committing; shadowing exposes false dreams cheaply.
principles.quote: Instead of just talking about it - take it for a 2 week test drive. **Try before you buy.**

principles.text: Those who survive the long flat stretch play to play, not to win; enjoying the game keeps you going.
principles.quote: The people that make it through the ‘decade of suck’ are the ones who enjoy the game. They don’t play to win, they play to play.

principles.text: Name and time-box a 'season of wandering' (3 to 12 months) to explore without prematurely committing.
principles.quote: **Give yourself a “Season of Wandering”** - take 3 to 12 months where you experiment & follow your curiosity. Test drive before you buy.

principles.text: Look for clues, not answers: find what feels like play to you but looks like work to others.
principles.quote: But the real clue is to figure out: **what feels like play to you, but looks like work to others?** That’s the moneymaker.

principles.text: Find blueprints: study people already living the life you want, and get specific about what you want.
principles.quote: The fastest shortcut in self improvement is to find someone who _already has what he wants_ and download the blueprint of their habits & mindset.

principles.text: Get outside your bubble and be near the people doing what you want; proximity reveals far more ways to win.
principles.quote: **Turns out there are 10,000x more “ways to win” than you even realized existed.**
